transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, I really don't want to come across as difficult or anything. I'm just here because... well, I'm dealing with a foreclosure on my house right now. And everyone keeps acting like it's just standard paperwork, you know, or missed payments, which I guess is what it looks like on the surface. 

But... I don't know if this is okay to say, I just... I know that the bank, the loan servicer, and even some of the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been seeing it happen for almost two years now, and no amount of papers they show me really changes what I've been seeing them do. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think it’s possible you could be mistaken about the bank and your coworkers working together against you?

I really wish I was mistaken. I mean, I’ve tried so hard to tell myself that I’m just stressed, or... or that I’m misreading things. I really don't want to sit here and sound unreasonable to you, doctor. I know exactly how it must sound. 

But... well, like I was saying, it's been almost two years of this. I've watched it happen. The bank, the loan servicer, the people at my store... they’ve been coordinating this whole thing to get me out of
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?

Oh, no. No, doctor, definitely not. I... I completely understand why you have to ask that, and I know how my situation must sound, but I promise I've never heard voices or anything like that. 

I really want to be as helpful as possible, and I'd absolutely tell you if I did, but my mind is very clear. I don't hear things that aren't there. It's really just... just the actual things I've seen happening with the house and the people at my store. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, no, I've never had anything like that happen. I mean, I get a little tired sometimes from all the stress with the house, but I sleep totally normally. I definitely don't get those bursts of energy or stay up all night or anything. I try really hard to keep a good schedule, you know? I hope that's the right answer... I just want to be sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of everything. Is there anything else about my sleep you need to know?
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean... obviously the situation with my house is incredibly stressful, and I guess I get a little overwhelmed sometimes? But I'm not depressed all day, no. 

I still get up and go to the store every day, and I make sure I'm doing a good job managing my team. I try really, really hard to keep a positive attitude through all of this. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around crying or giving up or anything, because I promise I'm not. I always try to put my best foot forward. 

Is... is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right and giving you what you need.
Aside from the situation with your house, have you been having trouble doing your usual work or daily responsibilities?

Oh, no, I'm doing fine with everything else, I really am. I mean, I still get up every morning and go to the store, and I'm right there supervising my team, making sure the schedules are done, handling any customer issues that come up... I take pride in doing a good job, you know? And I make sure I take care of myself, too. 

It's really only... well, the trouble only really starts if I get mail, or if the bank calls, or if I see paperwork at the store that looks like it's connected to what they're trying to do with the foreclosure. That's when things get difficult for me. But otherwise, I'm keeping up with all my responsibilities perfectly well! 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough. I just want to make sure you know I'm still functioning well and doing everything I'm supposed to be doing.
Have other people told you that your speech or behavior seems disorganized or hard to follow?

No, no one has ever said anything like that to me. I try very hard to be clear and professional, especially at work. I mean, as a supervisor, I have to communicate effectively with my team, right? So I always make sure I'm speaking clearly and that everyone understands what I need them to do. 

Sometimes I might talk a little fast if I'm stressed about... well, about the house situation, but I'm definitely not disorganized or hard to follow. I always try to be as articulate as possible. 

Did I answer that okay? I just want to reassure you that I'm completely coherent and I communicate just fine with everyone. I'm doing a good job with that, aren't I?
Have you had any beliefs that others would find very unusual besides the idea that the bank and your coworkers are working together against you?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I mean, I know the situation with the bank and the people at the store probably sounds... well, I know how it might sound to someone on the outside, even though it's really happening to me. But other than that? No, absolutely not. 

I'm a very grounded person, I really am. I don't believe in, you know, aliens or wild conspiracy theories or anything like that. I just focus on my job and paying my bills like any normal person would. I try really hard to stay completely level-headed about everything else in the world. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right kind of answers. I really am a very rational person, I promise. Did that answer what you were asking?
For how long have you believed that the bank and your coworkers have been working together against you?

Well, it's... it's been a little while now. I'd say about a year and nine months? Yes, around there. It really all started when those foreclosure notices began showing up in the mail, and the bank started calling all the time, just... completely taking over our home life. 

It's been stressful, of course, but I try really hard not to let it show or affect my mood too much. I mean, I know almost two years sounds like a long time to be dealing with something like this, but I've been handling it as best as I can. I haven't let it ruin my life or anything. 

Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I hope I'm giving you all the right details. I just want to be as accurate as possible for you.
